newsitem.title: USA: Marsh & McLennan, Johnson & Higgins agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Marsh & McLennan, Johnson & Higgins agree to merge.

text.p: Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc and Johnson & Higgins said Wednesday they had agreed to merge, "forming an enterprise that will be preeminent" in the businesses of risk and insurance services, consulting and investment management.

Under terms of a definitive agreement, Marsh & McLennan will acquire Johnson & Higgins for $1.8 billion -- one-third payable in cash and two-thirds in Marsh & McLennan common stock, a statement issued by Marsh & McLennan said.
The agreement has been approved by Johnson & Higgins shareholders and the Marsh & McLennan board.
Marsh & McLennan said the deal is expected to close in the second quarter, subject to certain conditions and regulatory approvals.
A new company, to be known as J&H Marsh & McLennan Inc, will be formed to manage the companies' combined insurance services operations. It will operate as a subsidiary of Marsh & McLennan.
Marsh & McLennan Chairman and Chief Executive A.J.C. Smith will hold those positions at J&H Marsh & McLennan Inc.
Johnson & Higgins Chairman and CEO David Olsen will become a vice chairman of Marsh & McLennan.
Marsh & McLennan said it had revenues of $4.1 billion in 1996, including $1.9 billion from risk and insurance services.
Johnson & Higgins had revenues of $1.2 billion in 1996, primarily from insurance-related operations, Marsh & McLennan said.
Both companies have consulting operations, accounting in 1996 for $1.1 billion in revenues at Marsh & McLennan and $110 million at Johnson & Higgins, Marsh & McLennan said.
Marsh & McLennan said it would finance the cash portion of the merger with bank financings and commercial paper.
